nodes.label: YOLO Unified Detection Pipeline Figure
nodes.description: The canonical YOLO 'The Model' schematic (dog-bicycle-car scene). A left panel shows the input image overlaid with an S x S grid; two outlined arrows fan out to an upper panel of many candidate 'Bounding boxes + confidence' with line thickness proportional to confidence and a lower panel showing a coloured per-cell 'Class probability map'; both streams converge through arrows into a right panel of 'Final detections' with three clean coloured boxes around the dog, bicycle and car.
nodes.rationale: The two parallel branches merging into one output is the whole argument of the figure: box regression and class prediction are produced by a single network pass over a grid, so detection becomes one regression problem rather than a proposal-then-classify cascade.

nodes.label: S x S Grid Division of Input
nodes.description: The input image is partitioned into an S x S grid; each cell is responsible for predicting boxes and class probabilities for objects whose centre falls in that cell.
nodes.rationale: Assigning responsibility by object centre gives each ground-truth object exactly one predictor, which keeps the loss well-posed and removes the need for external region proposals.

nodes.label: Bounding Boxes and Confidence Prediction
nodes.description: Per-cell regression of candidate box coordinates together with an objectness confidence score, drawn in the figure as box outline thickness.
nodes.rationale: Encoding confidence as a continuous score lets low-scoring boxes be pruned by thresholding and non-max suppression instead of by a learned second stage.

nodes.label: Class Probability Map
nodes.description: A per-grid-cell conditional class probability map, rendered as a coloured mosaic over the scene, predicted in the same forward pass as the boxes.
nodes.rationale: Predicting class per cell rather than per box keeps the output tensor small and fixed-size, which is what makes the single-pass real-time throughput possible.

nodes.label: Single-Stage Real-Time Object Detection
nodes.description: The design principle demonstrated by the figure: frame detection as a single regression from image pixels to boxes and class probabilities, evaluated in one network pass.
nodes.rationale: Chosen over two-stage detectors because one pass over the whole image gives global context and frame-rate inference suitable for constrained or embedded deployment; the trade-off is coarser localisation of small and clustered objects, which the fixed grid limits.
